scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. This is a really tough situation, and I'm not sure what to do. Let me try to break it down step by step. First, I need to understand the background. My girlfriend and I have been living together for two years. We moved to our current apartment a year ago because her sister, J, was always having people over, and we wanted more privacy. We moved out, and someone else took our spot there. Now, J has messed up her current living situation by not paying rent for two months. She owes about $3000, and her sister isn't sure if she'll ever pay it back. Because of this, J has come to live with us for free for about four months. J doesn't have a job and only sometimes helps with cooking. She parties a lot and comes home hungover. Our house has become a hangover den, which is not ideal. Plus, because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down, so she's not even looking for work. But that doesn't stop her from going out every other night to parties, which is concerning because if she gets sick from being reckless, it could affect us too. My girlfriend, L, doesn't like confrontation, so she hasn't opposed J living with us for free. But I can tell she wants J out too. I want my home back, and I've been trying to get L to talk to her about it, but she avoids confrontation. I'm conflicted because it's her sister, and I don't want to seem like a jerk, but it's gotten to the point where I might have to take the risk of L being mad at me. I think I might have to tell J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her own place, she needs to go back to her mother's. Is this the right thing to do? I need to consider several factors here. First, the financial aspect: J owes money, and she's not contributing financially to our household. Second, the impact on our living situation: our home has become a hangout spot for her friends, which affects our privacy and peace. Third, the emotional aspect: it's hard to kick out your own sister, and L might be upset if I do this. I also need to think about the long-term consequences. If I kick J out, what happens to her? She doesn't have a job, and she's not looking for one. She might end up back in a bad situation. On the other hand, if I don't kick her out, our living situation will continue to deteriorate, and it might cause more stress in our relationship with L. Maybe there's a middle ground. Could we set some boundaries? Like, J has to contribute in some way, or she has to look for a job. Or maybe we can give her a deadline to find her own place. That way, it's not just me kicking her out, but it's a mutual agreement. I also need to communicate with L about this. She's the one who's related to J, and she might have a different perspective. Maybe we can talk to J together and explain our concerns. It might be easier if both of us are on the same page. Another thing to consider is whether there's any way to help J get back on her feet. Maybe we can suggest she look for a job or offer some support in finding a place. But I'm not sure if she's willing to take that help. Overall, I'm torn between wanting to protect our home and maintain our relationship with L, and doing what's necessary to ensure our living situation is stable and peaceful. I need to find a way to handle this that respects everyone's feelings and needs.
